== Biography ==
John was born about 1824.<ref>Age 77 in 1901 census, age 82 at death 1906.</ref> He was the son of James Glasgow.

He passed away 6 May 1906 at Ballynasollus age 82, married (not widower). Attended by Ellen Glasgow, daughter.
<ref>[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/61a37b3461890 John Glasgow, 1906, Cookstown, 82] at Irish Civil Registration - Deaths</ref>
<ref>PRONI Will Calendars: Administration (with the Will) of the Estate of John Glasgow late of Ballinasollus County Tyrone Farmer who died 6 May 1906 granted at Armagh to Ellen Glasgow Spinster.</ref>
He was interred in Clare churchyard. The chief mourners were:
<ref>[https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0002006/19060512/069/0006 "Funeral of Mr John Glasgow, Ballynasollus"], ''Mid-Ulster Mail'' - Saturday 12 May 1906, Page 6</ref>
* [[Glasgow-1795|Thomas Glasgow]] (brother)
* Walter Glasgow, James Wright (sons-in-law)
* Robert Glasgow, Samuel Glasgow, Nelson Glasgow, W Glasgow (grandsons)

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1702]] is assessed at 93% (proved). John’s 1906 funeral names brother Thomas. His daughter Ellen of Ballynasollus attended James-1702’s widow Nancy at her 1916 death as granddaughter; another daughter Jane’s funeral calls Cunningham Glasgow her cousin. Together the named descendants, locality and brother link identify James’s family and support John as his son.

Confident93% as a combined family inference; Nancy may be a step-grandmother, James’s own father remains uncertain, and no direct John-son clause is claimed.

Next useful test: Verify Ellen’s informant wording and the named cousin chain beside the funeral’s brother clause.

Source basis already held: [https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0002006/19060512/069/0006 "Funeral of Mr John Glasgow, Ballynasollus" (https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0002006/19060512/069/0006), Mid-Ulster Mail - Saturday 12 May 1906, Page 6]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.



<blockquote>Administration (with the Will) of the Estate of John Glasgow late of Ballinasollus County Tyrone Farmer who died 6 May 1906 granted at Armagh to Ellen Glasgow Spinster.
</blockquote><ref>Northern Ireland, Wills and Administrations</ref>

<blockquote>
This is the last Will and Testament of me John Glasgow of Ballinalack in the County of Tyrone Farmer hereby revoking all other wills and testamentary dispositions heretofore made by me and declare this to be my last will and testament. I direct my Executors hereinafter named to pay all my just debts and funeral and testamentary expenses as soon as convenient after my decease. I give and bequeath to my wife Anne Jane Glasgow my farm of land and all houses and chattels which may belong to me thereon at the time of my death for and during her natural life, and after her death I give and bequeath the same to my four daughters [[Glasgow-1793|Jane Glasgow (abt.1855-1933)]], [[Glasgow-1798|Margaret Glasgow (bef.1864-)]], [[Glasgow-1715|Martha Glasgow (abt.1864-1935)]] and [[Glasgow-1713|Elenor Glasgow (1866-1927)]] share and share alike, subject to the payment by them of the legacies hereinafter mentioned. I bequeath to my son [[Glasgow-1732|James Glasgow (abt.1844-1906)]] of Killycurr the sum of five pounds and to my son [[Glasgow-1797|Nelson Glasgow (abt.1848-1921)]] now residing in Philadelphia in the United States of America the sum of five pounds but it is my will and wish that these legacies shall not be paid until after the death of my said wife. I appoint my said wife [[Ferguson-16492|Ann Jane (Ferguson) Glasgow (abt.1823-1912)]] and my daughter Jane Glasgow Executrixes of this my will. In witness whereof I have hereunto subscribed my name this 24th day of May 1905.

(Signed) John Glasgow

Signed by the said testator John Glasgow as and for his last Will and Testament in presence of us who at his request in his presence and in the presence of each other all present at the same time have hereunto subscribed our names as witnesses.

(Signed) John Johnston, Ballinalack
(Signed) Wm. J. Ferguson, Ballinalack

...after the expiration of one year after the death of my said wife Anne Jane Glasgow and in case the said James Glasgow and William Glasgow should die before my wife I direct that the legacies bequeathed to them shall go to their sons which are named after me and in case they should die before my wife then I direct the said legacies of five pounds each shall go to and belong to my four daughters in equal shares and if only one should die then the legacy of the one so dying shall go to my said four daughters in equal share alike. In case any of my said four daughters shall marry before the death of my wife or go to reside other than with my wife then I direct that the daughter so marrying or going to reside apart from my wife shall be paid the sum of twenty pounds or an equivalent of the value of my said farm of land after allowing for any debts then due by my wife at that date and the daughter receiving her share as aforesaid to have no further claim on my said farm. In the event of any of my said four daughters dying unmarried then I direct that the share of the daughter or daughters so dying shall go to and belong to the survivors in equal shares and if only one then the whole to such one. I direct that all the costs and expenses of burying my wife and all debts lawfully due by paying off the legacies hereinbefore bequeathed if my daughters on their marriage shall be paid by my said daughters or such of them as shall be residing with her at the time of her death in equal shares. I appoint Thomas John Gibson and Robert Allen both of Ballinalack aforesaid joint Executors of this my Will. In witness whereof I have hereunto subscribed my name to this my last Will and Testament this twelfth day of October one thousand eight hundred and ninety-nine.

John Glasgow

Signed by the said John Glasgow the Testator as and for his last Will and Testament in presence of us who in his presence and in presence of each other and at his request have hereunto subscribed our names as Witnesses (the words then I direct on first page being first struck out)

Wm Jas Allen, Cookstown, Clerk
Robert Allen, Ballinalack, Farmer

A. Wilson
Palmer W. 22nd Oct. 08 Dist. Reg.
</blockquote>

[[Glasgow-1702|James Glasgow (abt.1799-1882)]] identified as father, because John's daughter Jane is the cousin of [[Glasgow-701|Cunningham Glasgow]] at her funeral.

Corroborated by father James's second wife Nancy's death 1916 being attended by "Ellen Glasgow of Ballynasollus, granddaughter, 37" which can only be [[Glasgow-1713|Elenor Glasgow (1866-1927)]] .

Information from the will (1899):
* Wife: Ann Jane Glasgow.
* Four daughters, all unmarried: Jane Glasgow, Margaret Glasgow, Martha Glasgow, Ellen Glasgow.
* Son: [[Glasgow-1732|James Glasgow]] of Killycurragh.
* Son: Nelson Glasgow now residing in Philadelphia.
